slides.headline: The Hidden Risk Behind Derivative Margins

slides.title: Why Lower Margins Trap Retail Capital In Volatile F&O Markets

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: Lower margin requirements on longer-term derivatives mean cheaper leverage and safer directional trades.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: Lower margin simply increases leverage capacity, accelerating capital destruction when volatility strikes.

title_lines: Retail Capital In Volatile F&O Markets

slides.title: The Brutal Math Of F&O Losses In Modern Markets

stat_data.label: active retail traders losing capital in derivatives
stat_data.context: Recent regulatory disclosures highlight persistent compounding losses. Lowering margin barriers without structural risk education only deepens the drawdown loop for unhedged participants.

slides.title: How Smart Money Offloads Risk To Retail
flowchart_data: 1. Headline triggers sudden retail FOMO buying into momentum.
2. Institutions absorb retail liquidity to distribute heavy positions.
3. Volatility expansion triggers margin calls, wiping out leveraged accounts.

slides.title: The Hidden Drag Of Leverage Decay
slides.card_text: When margins are reduced, retail traders scale up position sizes beyond optimal risk parameters. This artificial expansion increases sensitivity to minor price retracements, leading to premature stop-outs and continuous capital erosion.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Execution Rule
slides.card_text: Never chase a headline move without verifying volume distribution and delivery percentages. Institutional accumulation leaves distinct footprints in order books that raw price action alone fails to reveal.
